data.narrative:
Valar Atomics is a Series B nuclear energy company valued at $6.0B post-money, having raised $1.0B to date. The nuclear energy sector comprises 11 peers total—3 public (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private entities including Oklo, X-Energy, Nano Nuclear Energy, Fuse Energy, and Aalo Atomics—though the narrow peer set within Series B or adjacent stages is limited.

Valuation analysis relied on stage-progression methodology, which applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B-to-subsequent-stage transitions. Applied to the $6.0B last post-money valuation, this method yields $11.4B. Peer-median analysis was not applicable due to insufficient comparable data points at the same stage or valuation tier; only 4 same-sector peers exist, with fewer than three meeting narrow filtering criteria. A broader all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given nuclear energy's distinct risk and growth profile.

The triangulated valuation range is $9.7B to $13.1B, with a median of $11.4B. This range reflects stage-progression mechanics alone, given the constraint on peer-based corroboration. Key uncertainties include regulatory trajectory, capital deployment efficiency relative to sector peers, and technology validation milestones. The narrow applicability of methods (one of two attempted) underscores the early-stage, capital-intensive nature of nuclear development and the limited public market depth for direct comparison.
